subject: Communication
title: Haptics: The Handshake as First Impression
description: A micro-lesson that makes Haptics: The Handshake as First Impression usable.

hook.text: A limp handshake cost one job candidate the position. The interviewer later said 'I just didn't trust him.'

buildup.text: Haptics — the study of touch communication — shows handshakes transmit information about personality and intent.

discovery.text: Research at the University of Alabama found handshake firmness predicts extraversion and emotional expression.

twist.text: The 'dominance handshake' (palm facing down) triggers resistance. Equal grip with vertical palms builds rapport.

climax.text: During COVID, handshakes disappeared. We discovered how much trust-building depended on that two-second ritual.

punchline.text: Two seconds of grip carry more than two hours of talk.

quiz.question: What does handshake firmness predict, according to research?

details.summary: Touch communication, or haptics, carries powerful social meaning. A firm handshake conveys confidence, while a limp one suggests weakness. Touch norms vary dramatically across cultures and contexts.
details.whyItMatters: A single handshake can set the tone for an entire interaction, making haptic awareness a practical communication skill.
takeaways: Haptics is the study of communication through touch
Handshake firmness influences first impression judgments
Touch norms vary widely by culture, gender, and setting

faq.question: What makes a handshake effective?
faq.answer: Research suggests a moderate grip, two to three seconds of contact, and one to two pumps create the best impression. Eye contact during the handshake amplifies its positive effect on perceived warmth and competence.

faq.question: How has the pandemic affected touch norms?
faq.answer: COVID-19 dramatically reduced casual touch and handshaking worldwide. Many people adopted elbow bumps or nods. While handshakes are returning, awareness of touch boundaries has permanently increased in many professional settings.
